title: Private Console — Upgrade Impact Simulator & Cost Forecast Card
creator: Priya Shah
description: Design and prototype a compact, actionable "Upgrade Impact Simulator" card for the Private/VPC Console cluster view. The card combines an interactive upgrade timeline with a cost-forecast widget and a network-aware risk slider so operators can preview the expected latency/SLO impact and marginal cost delta for an upgrade window before scheduling. Goals: 1) Surface trade-offs (latency vs cost) for different rollout strategies; 2) Provide network-aware gating recommendations (e.g., avoid canaries in AZ with >85% network saturation); 3) Enable exportable notes for release channels and automated rollout templates. The component should work at cluster and tenant scope, collapse into a single-line summary for dense dashboards, and expand into a step-by-step simulator with scenario controls.
comments: 2025-02-18 Priya Shah: Initial brief and sketching session. Focused on two views: condensed card (dashboard list) and expanded simulator (modal). Ran quick alignment with PM and Eng - priority is minimizing accidental SLA breaches during scheduled upgrades.

2025-02-21 Marcus Lee (Design): Low-fidelity prototype created. Key controls: rollout speed slider, canary size dropdown, network-sensitivity toggle, and a 'Simulate' button that produces two charts: SLO risk heatmap and marginal cost delta timeline.

2025-02-24 Engineering feedback (Rohit Patel): Backend needs an aggregated stats endpoint that can return sampled latency, token throughput, network saturation per AZ and projected delta for canary-induced load shifts. Suggested adding an ingest-limited simulation mode to avoid heavy compute at query time.

2025-02-26 Security review notes (Aisha Gomez): Concern about shipping raw tenant traces to simulator. Design decision: use sampled anonymized metrics and a redact+opt-in flow for deeper traces. Added requirement to surface data retention and opt-out information in the UI.

2025-02-28 PM review (Daniel Kim): Request to add cost unit breakdown (GPU-hours, network egress, storage snapshot ops) and show 95th percentile impact and median to capture tail risk. Also requested copy for 'What this means' microcopy for SRE audiences.

2025-03-01 Usability test (5 participants - infra SREs): Positive feedback on condensed card visibility. Pain point: users wanted clearer mapping between simulator steps and the resulting timeline events. Action: add event markers with hover descriptions and suggested mitigations.

2025-03-02 Marcus Lee: Updated high-fidelity prototype with event markers, exported JSON template for rollout API, and an accessibility checklist (contrast, keyboard flow, ARIA labels). Submitted design review request to PM/Eng.
Open items: confirm API contract for simulation inputs (ENG-4301 suggested), add feature flag for rollout, schedule dev spike to benchmark simulation latency.

Decisions: Use probabilistic model that runs on sampled metrics on the control plane with a 30s time budget. Favor predictive summaries (risk band + cost delta) over raw per-request playback to reduce compute and surface clarity for ops teams.
user_research: Recruitment: 5 infra SREs from two customers via Solutions Eng.
Key findings: operators want actionable recommendations (recommended canary size and safe window) instead of raw numbers; prefer default 'safe' presets but want quick toggles for aggressive rollouts.
Accessibility notes: all interactive controls must be keyboard operable and announce changes. Charts require text alternatives and CSV export.
Localization: copy reviewed for EN/FR; avoid idioms in microcopy to ease translation for APAC customers.
design_decisions: Show both 'Median' and '95th percentile' cost/latency forecasts to represent typical and tail behavior.
Network-aware gating: simulator highlights AZs with >70% baseline network utilization and recommends skipping or sequencing those AZs.
Privacy-first telemetry: simulation uses metric aggregates and sampled histograms. Deep trace mode requires explicit user opt-in and is logged for audit.
Collapsed card pattern: one-line summary with three bullets (expected SLA risk, estimated cost delta, recommended next step) to fit in cluster list without overflow.
Exportable rollout template: simulator produces a JSON template compatible with the rollout API to reduce copy/paste errors during scheduling.
tradeoffs: Real-time, per-request simulation is accurate but expensive; chosen to run a sampled probabilistic model with a bounded time budget to balance accuracy and cost.
Surface simplicity (recommended presets) vs flexibility (fine-grained controls). Default to safe presets with a prominent 'expert mode' toggle to reveal advanced options.
Per-tenant simulations increase privacy risk; decided to allow tenant-scoped simulation only for users with Auditor or Admin roles and log opt-ins.
Visualization density vs discoverability: condensed card avoids overwhelming dashboards but requires a clear expand affordance to surface details.
implementation_notes: Backend: need endpoint /api/v1/simulate-upgrade that accepts {cluster_id, rollout_strategy, canary_size, time_window, sample_rate}. Return summary bands and event timeline. ENG spike requested to estimate CPU/GPU cost.
Frontend: React component using existing charting lib (reusing Cluster Health sparkline tokens). Add ARIA attributes for controls and CSV download button.
Integration: wire 'Export to Rollout' to the rollout service; include a validation step to ensure templates respect customer quotas.
Data: use pre-aggregated histograms stored in metrics store (prometheus/histogram) and limit simulation to last-7d baseline by default.
Feature flag: console.feature.upgrade_simulator behind rollout-UX flag for staged rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Condensed card appears in cluster list with summary metrics and expands into simulator modal.
Simulator produces cost and SLO risk bands for default presets within 30s on staging data.
Exported rollout JSON validates against rollout API schema and pre-fills the rollout editor.
Accessibility checklist passed: keyboard nav, screen reader announcements, chart descriptions provided.
Security sign-off on data sampling/privacy text and opt-in flow.
